akhfash:3-3.t: He said ﴿قَدْراً﴾, and some read ﴿قَدَراً﴾; they are two dialectal variants.

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿مِّن وُجْدِكُمْ﴾: "الوُجْد" is means (ability); and some of the Arabs pronounce it with kasra in this sense. As for "الوَجْدُ", when you give the wāw a fatḥa, it is "love" (الحُبّ). In meaning — and Allah knows best — it is: "Lodge them where you dwell, from what you are able to afford" (أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنْتُم مِمَّا تَقْدِرُون عليه).

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ﴾: He made ﴿الأرْض﴾ a plurality, just as you say "هَلَكَ الشاةُ والبَعِيرُ" ("the sheep and the camel have perished") while you mean all the sheep and all the camels.*
